A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Scaling Laws for Black-box Adversarial Attacks. All 16 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack-success and loss measurements on image classifiers, defended models, and multimodal models, alongside optimizer comparisons and perturbation visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including Tables 1–3, the scaling-law plots, and the image-generation examples in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The ensemble attack objectives, SSA-CWA procedure, CLIP embedding adaptation in Section 4.1, and Algorithm 1 in Appendix C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same NIPS17 data, five target classes, classifier and multimodal evaluation scenarios, untargeted attacks, and Appendix F image-generation examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MI-CWA versus SSA-CWA, Figure 2 retains CWA versus MI-FGSM, and Figure 7b retains MI-CWA, VMI-CWA, MI-SVRE, and MI-FGSM. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The 100-image sample, 224×224 preprocessing, ensemble configurations, attack budgets, iteration counts, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendix D and Figure 9 retain the same evaluation prompts.

E4.justification: The gradient-conflict analysis, untargeted and optimizer comparisons, perturbation visualizations, curve-fitting analysis, and Appendix F case study are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Random ensemble selection and discussion of variability are unchanged. Neither version reports explicit repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains GPT-4o's cat-target ASR of 0.58 at epsilon 8/255 and 0.99 at 16/255 under Metric 2; the scaling curves and Appendix F examples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, Theorems 1–2, their assumptions and remarks, the mathematical objectives, and the Appendix A proof are unchanged. Opening-page reflow does not alter their content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about ensemble scaling, adversarial transferability, attacks on proprietary multimodal models, and semantic interpretability.

C2.justification: The interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including ASR saturation, the mismatch between pretrained models and the theoretical independence assumption, and explanations of gradient conflict and perturbation semantics.

D1.justification: v3 adds a page-1 footnote identifying the authors' ScaleUpAttack code repository, which v2 does not provide. Hyperparameters, pseudocode, model lists, and evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning, including Appendix G, are unchanged. Reference-list edits only update citation-page back-references for references 57 and 81.

P1.justification: v3 adds an explicit equal-contribution note and code-access sentence, and updates version/date information and footnote markers. The body prose, terminology, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added first-page footnotes cause localized text reflow across pages 1–3, and existing numbered footnotes switch to symbols. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: The new implementation-repository reference improves code discoverability and reproducibility documentation, while the equal-contribution note clarifies attribution. This is a limited documentation improvement: the scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
